# opusdns_email_forward (Resource)

Manages email forwarding for a hostname in OpusDNS.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opusdns_email_forward" "example" {
  hostname = "example.com"
  enabled  = true

  aliases = [
    {
      alias      = "info"
      forward_to = ["admin@mycompany.com"]
    },
    {
      alias      = "*"
      forward_to = ["catchall@mycompany.com"]
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hostname` (String) The hostname to enable email forwarding for (e.g., `example.com`). Semantic equality is used so the trailing dot the API serialises (`example.com.`) is treated as equivalent to the user-supplied form.

### Optional

- `aliases` (Attributes List) The list of email aliases for this hostname. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--aliases))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether email forwarding is active. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `email_forward_id` (String) The unique identifier for the email forward.
- `id` (String) The email forward ID.

<a id="nestedatt--aliases"></a>
### Nested Schema for `aliases`

Required:

- `alias` (String) The alias part (e.g., `info` for `info@example.com`). Use `*` for a catch-all.
- `forward_to` (List of String) The list of destination email addresses.

Read-Only:

- `alias_id` (String) The unique identifier for this alias.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import opusdns_email_forward.example <email_forward_id>
```
